title: BP delivery must release O across commit and receipt I/O
detail: REAL at 530f44d08. fnn-bpapp-deliver already calls fnn-owner-held-commit. That macro runs held-start under O, executes the preceding job off O, then runs the complete caller body under O in its second quantum. Both the START drain and the caller own submission can reach fnn-owner-statement-barrier. The current held plan labels the indivisible :submit effect :owner; it does not split that effect.
fix: Extend the held plan and host continuation together across the own submission and statement-bearing drain: capture under O, execute only immutable I/O jobs off O, settle under O, and retain the application plan and reader snapshot until durable resolution and receipt publication finish. Reapplying the already-present held-commit wrapper cannot remove this class.
notes: Statement first, lock-r2-class, 2026-10-08; traced checkout 414aed260. No numbered identifier required for descriptive LOCK repair IDs.
The cited fnn-owner-held-commit host macro is absent from this checkout; lane-commit-held-host contains an implementation to inspect as an integration dependency.

Full trail correction: most scoped durable I/O does NOT go through commit-queued-locked. It goes through fnn-owner-complete-bound-submission -> fnn-owner-attempt-served -> fnn-owner-attempt-filled -> fnn-owner-statement-committed -> fnn-owner-statement-barrier -> fnn-log-commit-open-batch. Thus lane-commit-held-host alone cannot drain the class: it moves the preceding queued batch, then executes the caller own submission body inside O again.

No BP host edits made. Its nine scoped keys remain. Required model work covers the caller own submit/take/intent/Store append and fence/resolution/publication, with the held gate keeping mutable application state coherent across each off-owner effect. The O pread trail additionally enters generic fn-owner-step through a fixed BP submit event; any path-sensitive GAP claim needs proof of the actual event restriction, not an informal reachability assertion.

Existing held-commit lane was inspected, not copied into this worktree; its host changes overlap C integration and do not solve the own-submission path above. Natives for C after a full split: tests.test_native_bp_app_clock, tests.test_native_bp_app_tally, tests.test_native_bp_transit_identity, tests.test_native_owner_scheduler, tests.test_native_slow_disk.

Round 2: waits on lane commit-held-host, which exclusively owns host/native/owner.lisp and host/native/bp-app.lisp now. Neither file is edited here. Dependency includes inline own-submission and identity/retention publication, not only the preceding queued batch. IO append registration must run in the same off-O held phase, with observation fed back before publication.

lock-classes statement-first review, HEAD 530f44d08: fnn-owner-held-complete sends :completed (or :completed-stopping); fnn-owner-held-frames-complete sends :frames-fenced on success. fn-och-step answers :submit with phase :idle and held=nil in either successful arm. fn-och-action-effects labels :submit as :owner; fnn-owner-held-commit invokes its body inside the second section. Thus running that body off O without extending the protocol would release the semantic hold as well as O, exposing the app plan and canonical Store to another writer.

Successor statement S0: for every observation sequence and admitted BP request (including duplicate, busy, refused, clock-unusable, uncertain and key-statement paths), projecting the new labelled continuation run to durable effects, application answers and final owner/Store/FNRJ state equals the current sequential application run. The same claim must cover each statement-bearing member encountered by held-start, not only the caller own submission. No event-specific unreachability is assumed for the generic fn-owner-step seam.

Successor statement S1: after the preceding batch or frames job completes, acquire/retain a uniquely owned submission continuation before any O release. Its identity, app plan, pending transaction, journal publications, reader snapshot and borrowed resources remain joined to the same owner value until terminal settlement. While a continuation exists, the committer cannot START, collect it or START-NEXT; no other writer changes the joined state. Reader quanta use only the captured committed view; every permitted reader/inspection step preserves the continuation invariant. Reject stale or duplicate effect receipts without mutation.

Successor statement S2: the host-called plan labels every semantic capture/settlement :owner and every FNRJ/FNFD publication, log registration, extension, append, barrier and cold read :off. For append register/write, K must also be off. A statement record is fenced before its key executor starts; the executor resulting identity publication is itself fenced before the next member or submission observes it. Refusal before effect, ambiguous persistence failure, core fault, stopping and process death have distinct successors; an ambiguous effect retains the intent and enters recovery, never successful rollback.

Successor statement S3: application context and receipt prepare/decision can publish only from the exact persisted Store result. No accepted reply or committed receipt leaves before its own required durable cuts. Include positive witnesses for a statement-bearing queued member followed by the held BP request and for a duplicate receipt; wrong-answer witnesses must submit after failed fence, release the hold before a write returns, run registration under O or K, execute a key change before its statement fence, substitute a receipt identity, and replay a stale completion. These are required successor statements, not admitted events or a certification claim.

Required host continuation cut map: split fnn-owner-commit-start-locked -> fnn-owner-drain-one at statement-committed; split fnn-owner-complete-bound-submission and fnn-owner-complete-bp-transit-submission at intent flush, Store attempt (including statement/key subcommits), resolution flush and outcome; split fnn-bpapp-accept-locked at request intent, Store submission, exact context bind and receipt decision. Shared publications used by retention/identity/control must use the same continuation before the IO class can drain. No host code or lock contract is changed in this review; this class remains open.

Final retained-tree lock comparison against 530f44d08: 234 keys have identical per-key site counts; 0 keys removed, 0 added, 0 counts rising, 0 NEW outside coordinator lock-dev-keys.txt (including its explicit ENCLAVE row). Full lock gate remains red: 52 new keys, 15 stale. Report: build/lock-classes/lock-comparison.json; printed counts: build/lock-classes/site-counts.txt. This class is not READY.
